title: Mexico Eliminates 88% of Consumption of Substances That Damage the Ozone Layer
author: Fernanda Monroy
content:
_This article by[Fernanda
Monroy](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/fermonroy/) originally appeared in
the [November 6, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/mexico-elimina-88-del-
consumo-de-sustancias-que-danan-la-capa-de-ozono/), a Mexican investigative
journalism magazine._

**Mexico eliminated 88 percent of its consumption of hydrochlorofluorocarbons
(HCFCs)** relative to its national baseline, as of December 2025, and
maintains the goal of their total elimination by 2030, reported the
Undersecretary of Environmental Regulation, **Ileana Villalobos Estrada** ,
during the 38th Meeting of the Parties to the Montreal Protocol (MOP38), held
from November 2 to 6 in **Kigali, Rwanda.**

Representing the Secretary of Environment and Natural Resources, **Alicia
Bárcena Ibarra** , the official presented **Mexico 's progress in eliminating
substances that deplete the ozone layer** and in the transition toward
refrigeration technologies with lower environmental impact.

According to Undersecretary Villalobos Estrada, as part of the implementation
of the Kigali Amendment, since 2024 Mexico has applied national control
measures and an import quota system for hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), with the
goal of freezing their consumption and advancing in their gradual reduction.

The undersecretary also presented the progress in the technological conversion
of the national refrigeration industry. Among them, she highlighted the
projects to replace refrigerants with high global warming potential with
natural alternatives.

Likewise, she reported that in 2025 the conversion of the national
manufacturing sector for self-contained commercial refrigeration equipment was
completed, through the incorporation of alternatives with lower climate impact
and improvements in energy efficiency.

During her participation, the official noted that the Mexican government is
promoting a **Humanist Ecological and Environmental Policy** that places
people and ecosystems at the center of public decisions.

According to what she presented, this orientation seeks to **link
environmental protection with the well-being of the population** and to
promote a technological transition that contributes both to the protection of
the ozone layer and to climate change mitigation and adaptation.

Ten years after the adoption of the **Kigali Amendment** , the official
highlighted multilateral cooperation as a tool to address environmental
challenges. The agreement establishes the gradual reduction of HFCs, used in
various refrigeration and air-conditioning systems and with a high global
warming potential.

Undersecretary Villalobos Estrada reiterated Mexico's commitment to complying
with the Montreal Protocol and the Kigali Amendment, through the adoption of
sustainable technologies, increased energy efficiency, and the strengthening
of national capacities.
